After receiving the news of your pregnancy, the time you spend in front of the mirror might be accompanied by a bit of hesitation. Roots that have grown out, split ends that have lost their shape... You want to go to the beauty salon, but the voices of your grandmothers, neighbors, or "scary stories" from the internet echo in your mind: *"Don't cut your hair, the baby's life will be short\!", "Don't dye it, chemicals will pass to the baby\!"*.

Pregnancy is not a period when a woman should stop taking care of herself. On the contrary, being well-groomed to reconcile with your changing body and feel good has a positive impact on your psychology. But where does the myth end and the medical truth begin?

Let's find scientific answers to the most popular questions about hair care and build a safe beauty routine.Myth 1: "You cannot cut your hair during pregnancy"

This is one of the most widespread superstitions in Azerbaijan and many Eastern countries. According to beliefs, cutting hair shortens the baby's life or "cuts" their intelligence.

**Medical Truth:**
This belief has no scientific or biological basis.  - **Hair is lifeless:** The visible part of the hair consists of keratinized (dead) cells. Cutting hair is like cutting nails; it does not create any physiological reaction in your body or the baby in your womb.
  - **Hormonal change:** In fact, during pregnancy, hair does not enter the shedding phase (telogen) due to the effect of the estrogen hormone and becomes thicker. However, if the ends are breaking, cutting them will help the hair look healthier.Conclusion: **You can cut your hair without fear.** This will not affect your baby, only your mood – and in a positive way\!Question 2: Is dyeing hair dangerous?

This issue is a bit more complex because it involves chemical substances.

**Scientific approach:**
The amount of chemicals in hair dyes absorbed into the blood through the skin is very minimal. Most studies conducted show that dyeing hair during pregnancy does not negatively affect the fetus or cause developmental defects.

However, following the principle of **"better safe than sorry,"** doctors recommend adhering to certain rules.1st Trimester Rule: Waiting

The first 12 weeks of pregnancy (1st trimester) are the most sensitive period when the baby's organs are forming. Although the risk has not been proven, most doctors advise refraining from dyeing hair **until the 12th week**.5 Golden Rules for Safe Dyeing (After the 12th week)

If you have decided to dye your hair, follow these safety measures:1.  **Choose ammonia-free dye:** Strong-smelling ammonia vapors can increase your nausea. Prefer organic or plant-based dyes.
2.  **Reduce skin contact:** Try to avoid the dye touching the scalp directly. Techniques like **balayage, ombre, or highlights** are the safest options because the dye is applied only to the hair strands, not the skin.
3.  **Ensure ventilation:** Make sure the salon is well-ventilated. Inhaling chemical odors is harmful.
4.  **Don't extend the time:** Keep the dye on the hair for the minimum time indicated in the instructions.
5.  **Wear gloves:** If you are dyeing it yourself at home, be sure to use gloves.Keratin and Botox: Is straightening allowed?

Hair straightening procedures (Keratin, Botox, Nanoplastica) are usually **not recommended**.  - **Reason:** Many keratin products contain **Formaldehyde** (or substances that turn into formaldehyde when heated). Formaldehyde is a carcinogen and enters the body through the respiratory tract when it evaporates. This is risky for both mother and baby.**Alternative:** Straighten your hair with a blow dryer or reduce frizz by caring for it with natural oils (coconut, argan).Henna and Natural Dyes

If you are concerned about chemical dyes, our grandmothers' method of **Henna** and **Basma** is the safest alternative. Natural henna is completely harmless, strengthens the hair, and gives it shine.  - **Attention:** Stay away from packaged "black hennas," as they may contain chemical additives like PPD (para-phenylenediamine).How will your hair change during pregnancy?

Pregnancy can be the "golden age" of your hair. Many women note that during pregnancy, their hair becomes less oily, shinier, and thicker.  - **Reason:** The estrogen hormone stops the hair loss phase.
  - **After birth:** Unfortunately, 3-4 months after birth, when hormones return to normal, those "saved" hairs will start to shed en masse. This is temporary and transient, do not panic.It is your right to look beautiful during pregnancy, and this is important for your psychological well-being. Cutting hair is completely safe, and dyeing hair is possible within certain rules (after the 12th week, ammonia-free).

Believe in scientific facts, not myths. Every moment you feel happy, you pass happiness hormones to your baby as well.
